final.memo:
Charlie and I have always maintained that we do not forecast markets; we simply look for businesses that we understand, that have durable moats, and that can be bought at prices offering a clear margin of safety. Today, the arithmetic of the market is unappealing. With the S&P 500 trading at roughly 28 times earnings and offering an earnings yield of 3.51%, stocks are expensive relative to the 4.37% yield available on a 10-year Treasury bond [D04, D06]. When our risk-free alternatives yield more than the earnings yield of the broad market, the hurdle for new equity commitments is exceptionally high.

We are currently in a state where our cash pile is large, but our opportunity set is small [D03, D08]. This is not a macroeconomic prediction or a signal that we expect a crash; it is simply a recognition that we are not seeing wonderful businesses at prices that make sense for a company of our scale [D01, D07, D08]. We will continue to hold our cash and short-term bills, waiting for a time when Mr. Market becomes more pessimistic and offers us assets at prices that reflect a true margin of safety [D01, D04]. In the meantime, we will remain disciplined, avoiding the institutional imperative to deploy capital just for the sake of activity [D01, D04].
